claims.text: Systematically adjusting the relative concentrations of magnetic elements in non-equiatomic HEAs modulates magnetic exchange interactions.
Modulating magnetic exchange interactions through compositional adjustment shifts the Curie temperature.
Compositional adjustment alters the magnetocaloric effect.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA contains both magnetic and non-magnetic elements.
Controlled thermal and environmental synthesis conditions promote homogeneous phase formation.
Controlled thermal and environmental synthesis conditions minimize segregation.
Altered elemental ratios induce chemical disorder.
Altered elemental ratios induce lattice distortions.
Changing the relative amounts of magnetic elements modifies interatomic distances.
Changing the relative amounts of magnetic elements modifies local bonding environments.
Changes in interatomic distances and local bonding environments alter magnetic exchange interactions.
Altered exchange interactions change the Curie temperature.
Changing the magnetic phase transition affects the magnitude of the magnetocaloric magnetic entropy change.
Increasing the content of the primary magnetic element elevates the Curie temperature relative to the baseline composition.
Increasing the content of the primary magnetic element enhances the magnetic entropy change relative to the baseline composition.
Reducing the content of the primary magnetic element lowers the Curie temperature relative to the baseline composition.
Reducing the content of the primary magnetic element lowers the magnetic entropy change relative to the baseline composition.
The compositional tuning effect is expected to be significant in low-dimensional, uniformly structured HEAs.
Phase segregation can limit the observed compositional tuning of magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
Additional anisotropic effects can limit the observed compositional tuning of magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
